name: X-linked Myopathy with Excessive Autophagy
aliases: X-linked Myopathy with Excessive Autophagy Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for X-linked Myopathy with Excessive Autophagy

criteria.description: Progressive proximal muscle weakness predominantly affecting males with onset in childhood or early adulthood
Muscle biopsy showing excessive autophagic vacuoles with sarcolemmal features and absence of acid phosphatase activity
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the VMA21 gene (X-linked)
Mild to moderate elevation of serum creatine kinase levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive proximal muscle weakness in males with confirmatory muscle biopsy findings and identification of pathogenic VMA21 gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; muscle biopsy findings are characteristic but not exclusive.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically affects shoulder and hip girdle muscles
searchTerms: gradual weakness of shoulder and hip muscles

pathognomonic.symptomName: Excessive autophagic vacuoles in muscle fibers
searchTerms: too many waste-filled compartments in muscle cells

pathognomonic.symptomName: X-linked inheritance pattern with male predominance
pathognomonic.notes: Family history often reveals affected males
searchTerms: X-linked inheritance with mostly males affected

common.symptomName: Mild to moderate serum creatine kinase elevation
common.notes: Usually less than 5 times upper limit of normal
Shows small polyphasic motor unit potentials
Due to weakness of periscapular muscles

searchTerms: mild weakness in hands and feet

occasional.notes: May cause exertional dyspnea in advanced stages
Develops in some patients with disease progression

rare.notes: Very rare; may present as dilated cardiomyopathy
Reported in isolated cases, unclear association

laboratory: Mild to moderate elevation of serum creatine kinase
Normal to mildly elevated lactate dehydrogenase
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective involvement of proximal muscles with fatty replacement
Chest imaging may reveal diaphragmatic weakness in advanced cases
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating excessive autophagic vacuoles with sarcolemmal features and absence of acid phosphatase activity

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier onset in infancy or childhood
Presence of acid phosphatase-positive autophagic vacuoles
Muscle biopsy shows dystrophic changes without excessive autophagy

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness with respiratory compromise
Family history of affected males with early onset weakness
Muscle biopsy showing excessive autophagic vacuoles
references: Nishino I et al. X-linked myopathy with excessive autophagy: a new type of vacuolar myopathy. Ann Neurol. 2000.
Schoser BG et al. Clinical and genetic spectrum of X-linked myopathy with excessive autophagy. Neurology. 2007.
Orphanet: X-linked myopathy with excessive autophagy (ORPHA:25980)
